facts.t: An American President cannot dissolve Congress
facts.d: No mechanism exists — a hostile legislature simply stays for its full term. Indian, British and French executives can all engineer dissolution, which is why gridlock in Washington resolves only at fixed intervals.

facts.t: France runs two executives at once
facts.d: A directly elected President who cannot be censured by the Assembly, alongside a Prime Minister who can. When they come from opposing parties the arrangement is called cohabitation — a constitutional situation with no Indian or American parallel.

facts.t: Britain only separated its top court in 2009
facts.d: Until then the highest appellate body was a committee of the House of Lords, sitting in the legislature. The Constitutional Reform Act created a separate Supreme Court — Britain's one deliberate concession to a doctrine it otherwise rejects.

bank.q: Which country is described as having fused powers?
bank.e: The United Kingdom — the executive is drawn wholly from Parliament and Parliament remains supreme.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about executive dissolution of the legislature:
s: The Indian President dissolves the Lok Sabha on ministerial advice.
The American President cannot dissolve Congress.
The French President may dissolve the National Assembly.
bank.e: All three are correct — the United States is the sole outlier, by design.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (mechanism of judicial review):
pairs: 1. No formal review, owing to parliamentary supremacy
3. Kesavananda Bharati and the basic structure
bank.e: India through Kesavananda, the United States through Marbury, the United Kingdom with no formal review, and France with a priori Constitutional Council review.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT true of the French system?
o: It has a dual executive of President and Prime Minister
The Assembly may censure the Prime Minister
The Assembly may censure the President
The President may dissolve the National Assembly
bank.e: The directly elected President is not subject to censure by the Assembly — only the Prime Minister is.

bank.as: India is described as having functional interdependence rather than strict separation.
bank.rs: Ministers are members of the legislature, and the judiciary has assumed quasi-legislative functions through public interest litigation.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The result is a cooperative model rather than the competitive one the American design produces.

bank.q: With reference to legislative control over the executive, consider the following:
s: It is high in India through questions, motions and committees.
It is complete in the United Kingdom, since the Prime Minister is directly accountable to Parliament.
It is high in the United States through frequent no-confidence votes.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. American congressional control is limited to the budget, confirmations and impeachment — there is no confidence mechanism.

bank.q: During an emergency, separation of powers is most fully overridden in:
bank.e: Articles 352 to 360 permit a comprehensive override. American checks survive through instruments like the War Powers Act; British parliamentary supremacy is unaffected; France sees significant but bounded centralisation.

bank.q: All of the following describe overlap between organs EXCEPT:
o: British executive drawn entirely from Parliament
American Cabinet members sitting in Congress
French Prime Minister answering to Parliament while the President does not
bank.e: The Incompatibility Clause bars any officer of the United States from sitting in either House — this is the one system with no such overlap.

bank.q: Which of the following best characterises the American model in practice?
o: Rigid separation producing a competitive model
A balanced hybrid with a dual executive
bank.e: Rigid separation, deliberately competitive. The other three describe India, the United Kingdom and France respectively.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the removal of the executive:
s: India uses a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha.
The United States relies on impeachment, which is rare.
France allows the Assembly to remove the President by censure.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Assembly may censure the Prime Minister, not the President.
